## Time Trends
- Upward/downward trends
- Seasonal patterns


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
evict %>%
  group_by(month_date) %>%
  summarise(avg_filings = mean(filings_2020, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = month_date, y = avg_filings)) +
  geom_line()
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](EDA_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-2-1.png){width=672}

**Summary:** There is no strong long-term trend in the filing data and very high month-to-month volatility.

```{.r .cell-code}
# Pull renter households data
renters <- get_acs(
  geography = "tract",
  variables = "B25003_003",
  state = "PA",
  county = "Philadelphia",
  year = 2023,
  geometry = FALSE
)
```

```
Getting data from the 2019-2023 5-year ACS
```

```{.r .cell-code}
renters <- renters %>%
  dplyr::select(GEOID, renters = estimate)

# Join to dataset
evict <- evict %>%
  left_join(renters, by = "GEOID")

# Normaliza filings
evict <- evict %>%
  mutate(
    filings_per_1k_renters = (filings_2020 / renters) * 1000
  )

# Compute tract-level average rate
evict_clean_rate <- evict %>%
  filter(!is.na(renters) & renters > 0)

evict_clean_rate <- evict_clean_rate %>%
  filter(renters > 100)   # adjust threshold

top10_rate <- evict_clean_rate %>%
  group_by(GEOID) %>%
  summarise(
    avg_rate = mean(filings_per_1k_renters, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_filings = sum(filings_2020, na.rm = TRUE),
    renters = first(renters),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(avg_rate)) %>%
  slice(1:10)

top10_rate
```

## Dynamics
- Create multiple lag variables (1 month lag, 1 quarter lag)
- Visualize Changes


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
evict <- evict %>%
  arrange(GEOID, month_date) %>%
  group_by(GEOID)

# 1 month lag
evict <- evict %>%
  mutate(
    lag_1m = lag(filings_2020, 1)
  )

# Quarter lag
evict <- evict %>%
  mutate(
    lag_3m = lag(filings_2020, 3)
  )

# Create change variables
evict <- evict %>%
  mutate(
    change_1m = filings_2020 - lag_1m,
    change_3m = filings_2020 - lag_3m
  )

# Visualize 1 month change
ggplot(evict, aes(x = change_1m)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 50) +
  labs(title = "Monthly Change in Filings")
```

**Summary:** Both monthly and quarterly change have symmetrical distribution. Eviction filings are not consistently increasing or decreasing. Changes in eviction activity fluctuate around a stable baseline rather than showing persistent growth or decline. This suggests that recent lag components of filings are strong predictors for future risks.

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
evict %>%
  group_by(racial_majority) %>%
  summarise(avg_filings = mean(filings_2020, na.rm = TRUE))
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
# A tibble: 4 × 2
  racial_majority avg_filings
  <chr>                 <dbl>
1 Black                  3.80
2 Hispanic               2.63
3 Other                  2.60
4 White                  1.70
```


:::
:::

**Summary:** Black-majority neighborhoods have substantially higher average eviction filings. Even after adjusting for renter population, eviction activity remains higher in Black-majority neighborhoods, suggesting structural disparities in housing stability.
